---
title: "max() of an empty vector is -Inf"
ref: NUM-13
categories: [Numbers]
impact: cryptique
extrait: 'max(numeric(0))'
reponse: '-Inf'
attendu: "`NA`, or an error"
versions: "All"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2021)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
grades <- c(12, 15, 9)
max(grades[grades > 20])
min(grades[grades > 20])
```
:::

## Why

The maximum of an empty set does not exist. R chooses to return the identity element of the maximum, `-Inf`, and `Inf` for the minimum, with a warning.

The case comes up after a filter that keeps nothing. `-Inf` is a valid number: it flows into the next calculations, shows up in a results table or blows up the scale of a chart, far from the cause.

## The remedy

Check the length before computing, and decide yourself which value to return.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
selection <- grades[grades > 20]
if (length(selection) > 0) {
  max(selection)
} else {
  NA_real_
}
```
:::
